text: Quinoa is a complete protein containing all nine essential amino acids. One cup of cooked quinoa has about 8 grams of protein and 5 grams of fiber.
Chicken breast is one of the leanest protein sources, with roughly 31 grams of protein and 3.6 grams of fat per 100 grams when grilled without skin.
Brown rice provides complex carbohydrates and 3.5 grams of fiber per cooked cup, making it a slower-digesting energy source than white rice.
Avocados are high in monounsaturated fats and potassium. Half an avocado contains about 120 calories and 6 grams of fiber.
Greek yogurt offers around 10 grams of protein per 100 grams, plus probiotics that support gut health. Choose plain varieties to avoid added sugars.
Salmon is rich in omega-3 fatty acids EPA and DHA, which support heart and brain health. A 100 gram fillet has about 25 grams of protein.
Lentils are an inexpensive plant protein: one cooked cup has 18 grams of protein, 16 grams of fiber, and significant iron and folate.
Almonds provide vitamin E, magnesium, and healthy fats. A 28 gram handful has about 6 grams of protein and 164 calories.
Sweet potatoes are high in beta-carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A. One medium sweet potato has about 4 grams of fiber.
Eggs are a versatile protein source: one large egg has 6 grams of protein and choline, which supports brain health.
